$description: Palette and scale primitives. Raw values with no meaning attached. Application code must never reference these directly; use the semantic roles in semantic.dark.json / semantic.light.json.

ink.$description: Dark-theme neutral ramp. Near-black surfaces, warm-neutral text. Steps 6 to 10 are the text ladder; 0 to 5 are surfaces.

6.$description: Disabled only. Below AA as text by design.

7.$description: Hints, placeholders, timestamps, footers: anything a person needs to read that is not body copy

cream.$description: Light-theme neutral ramp. Warm cream chrome, white cards. Mirrors the ink ramp step for step.

0.$description: Content well. One barely visible step below the chrome, the same 1.03 luminance ratio as ink 0 to 1. Lighter than the #EDE9E4 the reference skin shipped, which is too dark for accent text.

6.$description: Disabled only. Below AA as text by design.

7.$description: Hints, placeholders, timestamps, footers: anything a person needs to read that is not body copy

red.$description: Brand accent, a crimson. Step 3 is the product accent and the primary button fill: white on it reaches 4.50:1. The vivid fill cannot be used as text on cream, so accent text has its own steps, tinted on dark (1) and shaded on light (4). Danger is a separate, truer red (scarlet) so a destructive state never reads as a link.

1.$description: Tinted. Accent text on dark surfaces.

2.$description: Hover for accent-coloured text and icons on dark

3.$description: Product accent. Icons, borders, active indicators, and the solid fill under a white label (4.50:1). The centre of the banner gradient.

4.$description: Shaded. Accent text on light surfaces: 4.50:1 on the page well, 4.62:1 on the chrome, 5.24:1 on white.

5.$description: Fill hover, and link hover on light.

gradient.$description: The logo's end colours, sampled in sRGB. They exist only to be interpolated between: nothing may reference them as a flat colour, which is what the no-primitive-token lint enforces. The display gradient runs between them through pink; the fill gradient holds the accent fill across its middle so text sits on the solid band.

green.$description: Status success. Lightest to darkest. Hue and chroma held; lightness fitted so text passes on every warm surface and on its own chip.

1.$description: Pastel. Large status surface and chip background on light (12% of the fill into white, OKLab).

2.$description: Chip edge on light (30% of the fill into white).

3.$description: Large-surface border on light (45% of the fill into white).

4.$description: Success text and graphics on dark.

5.$description: Fill, under a white label (4.63:1). The 3px edge on dark status surfaces.

6.$description: Success text and graphics on light.

7.$description: Chip edge on dark (40% of the fill into the dark card).

8.$description: Chip background on dark (26% of the fill into the dark card).

amber.$description: Status warning. Lightest to darkest, same construction as green.

1.$description: Pastel. Large status surface and chip background on light (22% of the fill into white).

4.$description: Fill, under a dark label. The 3px edge on dark status surfaces.

5.$description: Warning text and graphics on dark.

6.$description: Warning text and graphics on light.

scarlet.$description: Status danger. A true red, deliberately apart from the crimson accent. Lightest to darkest, same construction as green. Lighter reds drift toward coral on dark, so the dark text step sits at the minimum that still passes on its chip.

1.$description: Pastel. Large status surface and chip background on light (10% of the fill into white).

4.$description: Danger text and graphics on dark.

5.$description: Fill, under a white label (4.61:1). The 3px edge on dark status surfaces.

6.$description: Danger text and graphics on light.

stone.$description: Status info. A warm grey: the brand has no blue. Info surfaces and chips use the neutral surface ramp, so this carries text and fill only.

1.$description: Info text and graphics on dark.

3.$description: Info text and graphics on light.

paper.$description: Brand cream insert. Used for the paper panel treatment, never as a UI surface.

space.$description: Seven named steps, all multiples of 4. Pick the role, never the number. A value that is not on this menu is a design question, not a CSS decision. 2px is not a step: a component that needs it builds it in, after checking that it does.

micro.$description: Inside a control: icon to label, chip and badge padding

tight.$description: Button padding, between tightly related controls

snug.$description: Between related elements in a group

compact.$description: Dense content padding: table cells, list rows, toolbars

base.$description: Default gutter: card padding, grid gaps

hairline.$description: The only border width. Separation comes from hairlines, not weight.

edge.$description: A colour bar, not a border: the status edge on dark callouts and tiles, and the active nav marker.

mono.$description: The machine voice: code, identifiers, versions, tracked labels

text.$description: Type scale. Dense by design: base is 14px, not 16px, because these are operator consoles. Nothing a person reads goes below 11px; 10px is for tracked uppercase labels only.

2xs.$description: Tracked uppercase labels only, mono or sans. Never other text.

xs.$description: The floor for all other text: dense metadata, stat labels, chart axis labels

lg.$description: Between card titles and page titles; no fixed role yet

xl.$description: Page titles, list and detail pages alike. Stat figures

2xl.$description: Display. Not used in the consoles today
